newsitem.title: USA: New York deal to broaden use of managed care - NYT.
newsitem.headline: New York deal to broaden use of managed care - NYT.

text.p: An agreement reached by the administrations of President Clinton and New York Governor George Pataki would for the first time require most of New York's 3.5 million Medicaid recipients to enroll in managed care plans, The New York Times said.

In Tuesday's edition, the paper cited "officials involved in the negotiations," who said the state would begin enrolling recipients in some upstate counties into managed care plans immediately as it worked out details with the federal government on how it would phase in the programme for the rest of the state.
Clinton has already approved similar programmes in at least 12 other states, but the one proposed by Pataki would be by far the largest and most ambitious, the newspaper said.
The state has been lobbying the federal government for more than two years to approve a waiver of Medicaid's traditional fee-for-service method of paying medical bills, it said.
